Physics hand-checked: light is a transverse electromagnetic wave; in ordinary light the electric field vector vibrates in every direction perpendicular to the direction of travel; a polaroid transmits only the component along its transmission axis, so the emerging light vibrates in one direction only — plane polarised light. Only transverse waves can be polarised.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.
insider_note: Only transverse waves can be polarised — the phrase vibrations restricted to one direction is what carries the mark, not the word polaroid.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Light is a transverse wave. In ordinary light
the electric field vector vibrates in every
direction perpendicular to the direction of
The property of light by which these
vibrations are restricted to one direction
only is called polarization of light.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say what vibrates (the electric field vector) and what happens to it (restricted to one direction).
steps.why: Polarization only makes sense for a transverse wave, because only a transverse wave has a vibration direction perpendicular to travel that can be restricted. Opening with the ordinary-light picture makes the restriction visible.
common_mistakes: Writing that light itself travels in one direction. It is the vibration of the electric field vector that is restricted to one direction, not the travel of the light.
Leaving out the electric field vector and saying only that light becomes one-sided.

recall.must_convey: That in ordinary light the electric field vibrates in every direction perpendicular to travel, and polarization restricts these vibrations to one direction only.
accept: electric field vibrates in all directions
perpendicular to the direction of travel

steps.memory_tip: Ordinary light: the electric field vibrates every way. Polarised light: it vibrates one way.

steps.label: Unpolarised to plane polarised
lines: Ordinary light is unpolarised. When it
passes through a polaroid, the light that
comes out vibrates in one plane only. Such
light is called plane polarised light.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name the device (a polaroid) and the result (plane polarised light).
steps.why: The definition needs a concrete way to produce the effect. A polaroid transmits only the component of the electric field along its transmission axis, so what emerges vibrates in one plane — that is what plane polarised means.
common_mistakes: Saying a polaroid blocks all the light. It blocks the component across its axis and passes the component along it.
Calling the emerging light unpolarised. Ordinary light is unpolarised; the light after the polaroid is plane polarised.

recall.must_convey: That ordinary light is unpolarised, and passing it through a polaroid gives plane polarised light that vibrates in one plane only.
accept: comes out vibrating in one plane
reject: vibrates in every direction perpendicular to travel

steps.memory_tip: Polaroid in, one plane out — unpolarised light enters, plane polarised light leaves.
